# PhysicsSolver 〔BlitzLLVM〕

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Physics](Blitz3D-Physics)

</div>


```blitzbasic
PhysicsSolver:Void preset:Int32, world:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `preset` | In | Int32 | required | 0 to 3. |
| `world` | In | Int32 | `0` | The physics world, 0 (default) for the default world. |

## Description

**〔BlitzLLVM〕** This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Chooses how exact the solver is. Jolt has one rigid body solver, so a preset is a set of values for the commands below, not another algorithm.

| Preset | Velocity iterations | Position iterations | Substeps | Sleeping | Continuous by default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0` balanced (default) | 10 | 2 | 1 | normal | no |
| `1` fast | 4 | 1 | 1 | sooner | no |
| `2` accurate | 16 | 4 | 2 | normal | yes |
| `3` custom | what the commands below set | | | | |

Setting any of the values by hand switches to `3`. Preset `3` itself changes nothing. The values of fast and accurate are a starting point and may change.

## Differences

* The original has no such command. This is an extension; programs that use it do not compile with the original Blitz3D.
